title: Replay must prove same-bytes: replayOf echoes the original decision for conflicting command bytes
description: Filed by architect-bdaffeaf 2026-08-20 from worker-21246c33's measured deviation record on task-3544d11c (REVIEW handoff msg-67e9c893, verified against source): `replayOf` (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:256) looks up the durable decision by key {commandId, principalId, projectId}, refuses only a KIND mismatch (BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED), and otherwise returns the original decision as an accepted REPLAY — it NEVER compares requestBytes. Consequence, all bootstrap commands: a caller reusing a commandId with the SAME kind but DIFFERENT payload bytes receives the original result as "ok, REPLAYED" — authority echoed for a command that was never decided with those bytes (the recorded qa-replay-path-can-echo-the-caller class). The store's own requestBytes conflict arm exists but is UNREACHABLE through the daemon edge because replayOf short-circuits before any store write — the refusal-answered-by-earlier-layer pattern, here hiding a byte-compare instead of a refusal. No double-commit risk (effects are never re-run); the defect is HONESTY of the replay claim. OBJECTIVE: make the daemon replay path prove same-bytes before claiming REPLAYED — compare the canonical requestBytes (the same construction commitAccepted writes) against the stored decision's requestBytes; mismatch refuses with a stable exact code (e.g. BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT) at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, original decision bytes preserved untouched. Existing true replays (byte-identical) unchanged. NOTE: task-3544d11c's new suite asserts the CURRENT reachable behavior (conflicting resubmit replays) — that assertion must be updated by THIS row when the refusal lands, coordinate via its test file planning-authority-persistence.test.ts. Measure first whether the store's CommandDecisionRecord exposes requestBytes to the daemon read path; if not, the store read surface gains it (packages/store owned path added to scope at planning time).
definitionOfDone: replayOf (or its successor seam) compares canonical request bytes against the stored decision before returning REPLAYED; byte-identical resubmits replay exactly as today

A conflicting-bytes resubmit (same key, same kind) refuses with the exact new stable code at its named layer, original decision and result bytes preserved and asserted byte-identical after the refusal
Every bootstrap command kind inherits the check through the shared seam - proven by at least one second-kind case, not asserted from the roster
Focused tests use the real store + real sequence path with accepted control, replay control, conflict arm, and a mutation drill that neuters the byte-compare and reds a named test
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0 with nonzero counts; the 3544d11c suite's conflicting-resubmit assertion updated in the same slice so no suite asserts the old echo
taskRails: Never weaken the kind-mismatch guard (BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED) - the byte-compare is additive, ordered after it.
Original decision bytes are immutable evidence - the conflict arm must prove zero mutation of the stored row.
Re-measure replayOf at HEAD before planning (stale-by-default); 3544d11c may land first and its suite location is the coordination point.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASURE at HEAD (record commands+results). (a) replayOf (apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:256): confirms lookup by {commandId, principalId, projectId}, refuses ONLY kind mismatch (BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED), returns original as REPLAYED with no byte comparison. (b) WHY exact-preimage reconstruction is NOT the design: CommandDecisionRecordBase carries requestSha256 (store-contracts.ts:104) but its preimage (identifyExpectedVersionRequest, store-digests.ts:92-110) folds requestBytes together with expectedVersion, targetAggregateId AND per-leg fences {aggregateId, expectedVersion} — the record does not expose leg fences, and a multi-leg decision's fences cannot be rebuilt at replay time (the authority leg's version has advanced), so recomputation would false-refuse honest replays of exactly the decisions 3544d11c just landed. Verify leg fences are truly absent from the record read surface. (c) DESIGN D-A pinned: the store gains requestBytesSha256 — a domain-framed sha256 over requestBytes ALONE (own version const, identifyDecisionResult:112 is the shape precedent) — persisted with every decision and read back on both record variants; requestSha256 untouched. The daemon compares via a STORE-EXPORTED helper, never a local reimplementation (two-copies-of-one-rule drift, the 36a87add lesson). Measure the store's write path (decision-ledger-canonical.ts:89-94 identity assembly, decision-ledger-record.ts persistence/read mapping) and the DDL/column-evolution pattern for the new field; identify whether @moe/store's root barrel must gain the helper export. (d) LEGACY ROWS: pre-existing decisions have no stored digest — PIN the fail-closed choice: a null-digest row's replay proof is UNKNOWN and REFUSES with its own exact code (v0.2 dev-stage stores make this cheap; epic rail 4: unverifiable evidence never gains authority); record the choice for governor visibility. (e) COORDINATION: task-3544d11c status (REVIEW at claim time) — locate its conflicting-resubmit assertion in planning-authority-persistence.test.ts and record its landed form; this row owns flipping it (DoD 5). (f) Dependency-edge rail for @moe/store consumption from apps/daemon: manifest + lock importer + bare-specifier probe typecheck exit 0, probe deleted.

RE-MEASURED at HEAD a92544f. Commands+results:

No byte compare. runBootstrapCommand calls replayOf immediately after ingress decode (bootstrap-services.ts:201), before prerequisites and before any handler, so the new arm is reachable and unshadowed.

(b) CONFIRMED. identifyExpectedVersionRequest (store-digests.ts:92-110) folds expectedVersion + targetAggregateId + per-leg fences with the bytes. AdditionalLegFence (decision-ledger-fences.ts) is NOT on CommandDecisionRecordBase (store-contracts.ts:86-109 read in full - no legs field). Reconstructing requestSha256 is impossible for multi-leg. Plan premise verified.

(c) MEASURED DEVIATION - design D-A replaced by D-C. D-A (new durable requestBytesSha256 column) needs SQLite schema v7: sqlite-schema-manifest.ts uses EXACT-TEXT conformance (sqlite-schema-conformance.ts:45) and 5 foreign test files hard-pin 6 / "moe-sqlite-schema/6" (command-decision-integrity.test.ts:175, sqlite-event-store-core.test.ts:26, store-schema-v3-migration.test.ts:114, store-schema-v4-migration.test.ts:126-127, store-schema-v6-subscription-offers.test.ts:29-30) - plus it CREATES the legacy-row hazard step 1(d) wanted flagged to the governor.
D-C: the store ALREADY persists a bytes-covering digest for every decision. command_receipts.request_sha256 = identifyCommandRequest({aggregateId, expectedVersion, commandBytes}) and commandBytes === request.requestBytes on BOTH commit paths (store-input-decision.ts:104 snapshotCommittedProposal; decision-ledger-legs.ts:175 planLegsDecision - every leg). Its two co-inputs are the PRIMARY leg's aggregateId/expectedVersion, which ARE decision.targetAggregateId / decision.expectedVersion by construction. Recomputing that digest from the STORED co-inputs plus FRESH bytes leaves requestBytes as the only free variable => exact same-bytes proof, no leg-fence problem (fences never enter this preimage).
Reachability: decodeStoredCommandDecision already calls ctx.loadReceipt for EVERY decision (decision-read-decode.ts:163) and StoredReceipt carries requestSha256 (store-internals.ts:72-86); writeCanonicalDecision already holds effect.receipt (decision-ledger-record.ts:166). So write path and read path each gain ONE line - no SQL change, no migration, no version bump.
Tamper-evidence: loadReceipt re-derives identifyCommandEffects (event-read-materialization.ts:~232) which folds requestSha256 (store-digests.ts:221) and compares to effectSha256; the decoder cross-checks receipt.effectSha256 === decision.effectSha256; effectSha256 is folded into decisionSha256 (store-digests.ts:211). Chain already closed.

(d) LEGACY ROWS: MOOT under D-C. Every existing EFFECTS_COMMITTED row already carries the evidence, so there is no null-digest arm and no fail-closed refusal that would break pre-existing stores. This REMOVES the governor-visible hazard D-A would have introduced. NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT rows get null (their receipt covers the audit payload, not requestBytes) - and replayOf already returns null for them (:327), so nothing regresses.

(e) COORDINATION - STALE PREMISE. planning-authority-persistence.test.ts (3544d11c, landed 75aa463) has NO conflicting-resubmit assertion. Its only replay test is "replays a byte-identical resubmit without writing anything new" (:228), which stays green. DoD 5's flip has nothing to flip there. Cases as landed:
(a) REPLAY CONTROL — each swept kind first commits (DECIDED), then resubmits byte-identical and must get REPLAYED with identical result bytes. This is the negative control that stops a fix from degenerating into "always refuse".
(b) CONFLICT ARM — exact code BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, plus authority NONE / advisoryOnly true. Immutability of the original decision is proven by a before/after `snapshotDecision` toEqual over {decisionSha256, resultSha256, replayRequestSha256, decoded result}, not by an ok-check, and decision + event counts are pinned.
(c) SHARED SEAM — swept over THREE kinds: project.register, policy.install and plan.propose. plan.propose additionally commits through the MULTI-LEG seam (commitAcceptedLegs), so the sweep covers both commit paths at the daemon edge. Per epic rail 6 the sweep asserts it was actually generated: length 3, three distinct kinds, each entry's index really names that kind in bootstrapSequence(), and each conflicting payload really differs from the original.
(d) KIND-MISMATCH PRECEDENCE — the reused-id case deliberately changes BOTH the kind and the payload, so if the byte compare were ordered before the kind guard it would answer and BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_ID_REUSED would go silent. Already passing; it is the ordering trap, and drill (v) confirms it reds when the compare moves ahead of the guard.
(e) LEGACY ARM REPLACED, per the step-1/step-2 D-C measurement: no absent-digest row can exist. Its honest analogue is pinned instead — a decision with NO same-bytes evidence (a NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT row, written by the production `commitAccepted` seam under a stale fence, not forged) must make `replayOf` return null for the identical bytes AND for different bytes, so "no evidence" is never read as a match.

```
907d8f8 = 363    9b94112 = 363    ccff6bc = 376    15f5f8f = 376    7c9c786 = 376    HEAD = 376
```

363 is the count at 907d8f8 — this row's own deliverable commit — and it was accurate there. `ccff6bc` ("feat(daemon): the operator's own approval dispatch is the human review", `13 0` on this file) grew it by 13. That is a FOREIGN commit, not this row's; `git show --numstat` attributes the hunk to it directly. So the file gained 13 lines this row did not write, between the commit and the gate run.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR GRADING: the cap clause reads off the number. 363 presents as 113 under the 400 hard cap; 376 is 24 under. Still under, and still above the 250 target as already disclosed — the disclosure's substance is unchanged, its margin is not. QA should grade 376 at HEAD, or 363 at 907d8f8, but should not mix them.

Discipline: `git show <sha>:<path> | grep -c ''`, quote the SHA beside the number.
